documents.title: Artificial Intelligence at USD: Guidance and Principles
documents.summary: Central USD page on responsible GenAI use. It gives principles (human judgment, disclosure, verification, privacy, accessibility), names Microsoft Copilot as the approved tool, and leaves AI-use decisions to disciplines and courses.
documents.stance_why: The hub states principles but "should not be viewed as official policy; it is intended to provide guidance", and says "Faculty should make this determination in collaboration with peers" and that AI's "role will vary across disciplines, courses, assignments", so it sets no stance and hands the decision to faculty and courses.

units.why: Opening purpose statement: the page exists "to guide students, faculty, and staff in the ethical and innovative use of generative AI", an institution-level framework covering all audiences.
units.anchor: guide students, faculty, and staff in the ethical and innovative use of generative AI

units.why: Defines GenAI as "a type of artificial intelligence that uses large datasets to generate content", setting what the guidance covers; a definition so P61.
units.anchor: GenAI is a type of artificial intelligence that uses large datasets to generate content

units.why: FAQ definition lists "text, images, code, audio or video" and named tools ("ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini"), defining the scope of covered tools, so P61.
units.anchor: tools that can generate content
units.policy: GenAI refers to tools that generate content such as text, images, code, audio or video from prompts or questions, for example ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini.

units.why: States the university must help stakeholders "navigate this reality" of regular GenAI use, a rationale for engaging rather than banning. P82 is nearest (AI use is a fact that cannot be avoided); P87 (benefits) does not fit as no benefit is named.
units.anchor: people regularly use GenAI
units.policy: Students, faculty, staff and graduates live in a world where people regularly use GenAI, and USD must help them navigate it.
units.fit_note: Says AI use is a fact of the world that USD must help people navigate; it does not say use cannot be verified or prevented.

units.why: Says USD values promoting "technology literacy" and preparing the community for "the workplace"; an AI-for-careers rationale, P44.
units.anchor: preparing our community to be successful in the 21st century learning environment and workplace

units.why: Commits USD to "teach and empower" people to understand and "when appropriate, to utilize with care" GenAI; a qualified encouragement of use, nearest P02, though "when appropriate" defers to context.
units.anchor: when appropriate, to utilize with care the latest developments in technology, including GenAI
units.fit_note: Encouragement is qualified by 'when appropriate' and 'with care' and does not set a default for coursework.

units.why: "should serve as a supplement to human activity, not a replacement" says AI must not replace human thinking; P32 (human stays primary), not P29, because it is about the role of AI rather than ownership.
units.anchor: should serve as a supplement to human activity, not a replacement

units.why: "USD encourages transparency and accuracy" with "final work, decisions and strategies reflecting human judgment" asks for transparency about AI use; nearest P24, as an encouragement rather than a per-submission rule.
units.anchor: USD encourages transparency and accuracy in the context of GenAI use
units.fit_note: Encourages transparency in general terms without requiring a statement on each submission; also asks that final work reflect human judgment.

units.why: "expected to maintain professional and academic integrity when using these tools" is a general ethical expectation with no specific content, P116.
units.anchor: expected to maintain professional and academic integrity when using these tools

units.why: "should not be viewed as official policy; it is intended to provide guidance" states the status of the page as non-binding guidance; no type covers a document's self-declared status.
units.anchor: should not be viewed as official policy; it is intended to provide guidance
units.uncovered_note: The page declares itself non-binding guidance rather than official policy.

units.why: "GenAI can help individuals brainstorm, iterate, and explore multiple angles" permits brainstorming and exploring approaches, conditioned on questioning and verifying output; P15.
units.anchor: GenAI can help individuals brainstorm, iterate, and explore multiple angles

units.why: "GenAI can help explore scientific questions, identify patterns, test hypotheses and make sense of non-sensitive data" allows data exploration and analysis as part of learning; P89.
units.anchor: identify patterns, test hypotheses and make sense of non-sensitive data

units.why: "use human judgment to verify sources and results" is a verification duty; P31. The "treat sensitive data with care" half is coded under the privacy rule below.
units.anchor: use human judgment to verify sources and results

units.why: "Effective GenAI requires that users develop clear goals, craft well-structured prompts, fact check output" gives practical prompting advice, P93.
units.anchor: craft well-structured prompts, fact check output and reflect on their use of technology

units.why: "we recommend individuals use their critical thinking skills to assess, question and refine the GenAI answers" asks users to critically evaluate output, P31.
units.anchor: use their critical thinking skills to assess, question and refine the GenAI answers

units.why: "employers expect graduates to understand where GenAI can effectively assist" gives a professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: employers expect graduates to understand where GenAI can effectively assist

units.why: "USD prepares students to use GenAI ethically and competently" commits the university to teaching AI use as a workforce skill, P44.
units.anchor: USD prepares students to use GenAI ethically and competently

units.why: "USD uses Microsoft 365 Copilot as its approved GenAI chat" names the institution-wide sanctioned tool, P92 (institution-wide, not one course, so not P17).
units.anchor: USD uses Microsoft 365 Copilot as its approved GenAI chat

units.why: "We encourage faculty, staff and students to use this tool" is a recommendation to use the approved tool, P92.
units.anchor: We encourage faculty, staff and students to use this tool for GenAI chat functions

units.why: "view a list of AI tools approved for various uses and their security level in Coyote One Stop" points readers to further resources, P115.
units.anchor: view a list of AI tools approved for various uses and their security level

units.why: "Independent thinking and academic freedom remain central to learning" frames the learning rationale as protecting independent thought; P41 is nearest.
units.anchor: Independent thinking and academic freedom remain central to learning.
units.fit_note: Frames independent thinking as central; does not say AI shortcuts practice.

units.why: "USD supports the freedom to explore, debate, critique and discuss ideas ... and expects that freedom to be exercised with professionalism and responsibility" states an academic-freedom principle with a responsibility expectation, P116.
units.anchor: expects that freedom to be exercised with professionalism and responsibility

units.why: "AI is a university resource, not a technology mandate" and "not a requirement for every academic or professional pursuit": AI is optional. Nearest P51 (AI not required), though the passage is not about cost or access.
units.anchor: GenAI is a resource available to the university’s community, not a requirement
units.fit_note: Says AI is not required; the type centers on cost and equal access, which the passage does not mention.

units.why: "Its role will vary across disciplines, courses, assignments and/or projects" leaves the AI rule to be set per course or assignment, P04.
units.anchor: Its role will vary across disciplines, courses, assignments and/or projects.

units.why: "USD’s priority is maintaining the integrity of learning and inquiry while upholding the academic standards and expectations of individual courses": rationale grounded in integrity and course standards, P95 nearest.
units.anchor: maintaining the integrity of learning and inquiry while upholding the academic standards
units.fit_note: Also says individual courses' expectations govern.

units.why: "Accuracy requires human judgment": users should examine, verify and reflect on outputs; P31.
units.anchor: requires examining, verifying and reflecting on outputs

units.why: "Treating GenAI as a drafting or exploratory partner, rather than an authority" says output is not authoritative, so P31 (verify) fits.
units.anchor: Treating GenAI as a drafting or exploratory partner, rather than an authority

units.why: "USD will review this guidance regularly and update it" commits to regular review, P54.
units.anchor: USD will review this guidance regularly and update it

units.why: Principle 1 says deep learning comes from "responsible and ethical use" of technology to explore and critique ideas: an institution-level principle, P56.
units.anchor: Independent thinking and deep learning emerge from the responsible and ethical use

units.why: "Faculty should make this determination in collaboration with peers and academic leadership, guided by disciplinary norms, accreditation requirements and course outcomes": faculty decide AI use, so P04; peer alignment (P109) and course outcomes (P83) are secondary.
units.anchor: Faculty should make this determination in collaboration with peers
units.fit_note: Adds that faculty decide with peers and leadership guided by disciplinary norms, accreditation and course outcomes (P109, P83).

units.why: "AI use will vary both between and within disciplines" states that rules differ by discipline, P04.
units.anchor: AI use will vary both between and within disciplines.

units.why: "students, faculty and staff should disclose how it was used and cite sources or models where relevant" is a disclosure norm when AI contributes meaningfully, P24; "consistent with instructor/program guidance" defers detail.
units.anchor: students, faculty and staff should disclose how it was used and cite sources or models

units.why: "AI can be incorrect or biased. Users must validate claims with credible sources" requires verification and names bias; P31.
units.anchor: Users must validate claims with credible sources, note limitations

units.why: "avoid overreliance on AI for facts, analysis or authorship" warns against replacing own thinking, P32.
units.anchor: avoid overreliance on AI for facts, analysis or authorship

units.why: "Do not enter confidential, personally identifiable or proprietary information into AI tools without explicit authorization" is a privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: Do not enter confidential, personally identifiable or proprietary information into AI tools

units.why: "Respect creators’ rights and licensing" concerns IP, P52.
units.anchor: Respect creators’ rights and licensing.

units.why: "If used, AI should be deployed in ways that broaden access to all learning materials and support all learners" is an accessibility principle, P97.
units.anchor: AI should be deployed in ways that broaden access to all learning materials

units.why: "remain accountable for final decisions" makes users responsible for decisions informed by AI judgments; P29 is nearest, but it covers decisions generally, not only submitted work.
units.anchor: remain accountable for final decisions
units.fit_note: About accountability for decisions generally, not only submitted work.

units.why: "The first draft of this page was written with the assistance of GenAI ... reviewed and refined by USD faculty and staff" describes how the guidance was made, P84.
units.anchor: reviewed and refined by USD faculty and staff over the course of several months

units.why: "we encourage students to explore AI as a learning partner, not a replacement for their own thinking" encourages exploration while keeping thinking primary; P32 nearest.
units.anchor: we encourage students to explore AI as a
units.fit_note: Also encourages students to explore AI as a learning partner (P02-like).

units.why: "GenAI tools must be reviewed and approved before use on campus" requires institutional approval of tools, P65.
units.anchor: GenAI tools must be reviewed and approved before use on campus.

units.why: "USD’s Information Technology Department provides information on which tools have passed review" names IT as the reviewing office, P80.
units.anchor: Information Technology Department provides information on which tools have passed review
units.fit_note: IT also states what data is acceptable on each platform.

units.why: "Microsoft Copilot is the only tool on USD’s campus that is approved for full, integrated use" sets the one fully approved tool, P92.
units.anchor: Microsoft Copilot is the only tool on USD’s campus that is approved for full

units.why: "Other tools may be used as standalone platforms or for non-restricted data" permits other tools under a data limit, P92.
units.anchor: Other tools may be used as standalone platforms or for non-restricted data
units.fit_note: Permits unapproved tools only for standalone use or non-restricted data.

units.why: "use of AI may not be allowed in certain courses or appropriate in all contexts" tells people that course rules can ban AI, P04.
units.anchor: use of AI may not be allowed in certain courses or appropriate in all contexts

units.why: "AI-generated text should not be sent as-is" and AI is "a tool, not a replacement for human communication" covers authentic communication; P58 is nearest but it concerns course staff messages.
units.anchor: AI-generated text should not be sent
units.fit_note: Applies to communication in general across the campus community, not only messages to course staff.

documents.unit: University of South Dakota (AI hub, Faculty)
documents.title: Generative AI Information: Faculty
documents.summary: Guidance for faculty on setting expectations, using AI in teaching and research, protecting data, and responding to suspected misuse through process rather than detection tools.
documents.stance_why: The faculty page tells faculty to state in each syllabus "whether AI use is allowed, limited or prohibited" and sets no default of its own, so the decision rests with instructors.

units.why: Page purpose: "Learn how to use AI to support your teaching and research while staying true to your own ideas" is faculty-facing guidance that frames AI use in faculty work as welcome; P59.
units.anchor: use AI to support your teaching and research while staying true to your own ideas

units.why: Defines GenAI with examples "ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and discipline-specific AI tools", setting scope; P61.
units.anchor: tools that can create new content such as text, images, code, audio or video

units.why: "best positioned as supplements to human expertise and judgment, not replacements for faculty knowledge" says AI should not replace the human, P32.
units.anchor: supplements to human expertise and judgment, not replacements for faculty knowledge

units.why: "GenAI is part of the professional landscape our graduates will encounter" gives a career rationale for faculty engagement, P44.
units.anchor: GenAI is part of the professional landscape our graduates will encounter.

units.why: "please reach out to the Center for Teaching and Learning" points faculty to support, P63.
units.anchor: reach out to the Center for Teaching and Learning

units.why: "Faculty are responsible for clearly communicating expectations regarding AI use in their courses" assigns faculty the duty to state AI rules, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty are responsible for clearly communicating expectations regarding AI use in their courses.
units.fit_note: Duty to communicate expectations; the syllabus is named in the next item.

units.why: "If no guidance is provided, students may make incorrect assumptions about acceptable use" explains why silence is a problem; nearest P09, as no fallback rule is set (so not P06).
units.anchor: If no guidance is provided, students may make incorrect assumptions about acceptable use.
units.fit_note: Explains the risk of silence; does not define a fallback rule (P06).

units.why: "Stating whether AI use is allowed, limited or prohibited in each course syllabus" asks for an AI statement in each syllabus, P09; the allowed/limited/prohibited range is a spectrum of choices, not defined tiers (so not P05).
units.anchor: Stating whether AI use is allowed, limited or prohibited in each course syllabus.

units.why: "Identifying which tools are permitted" asks instructors to name permitted tools, part of the syllabus statement, P09.
units.anchor: Identifying which tools are permitted.

units.why: "Explaining disclosure or citation requirements" asks instructors to say how AI use must be disclosed, P09.
units.anchor: Explaining disclosure or citation requirements.

units.why: "Providing students with reasoning for why AI will or will not be used" asks instructors to explain their rules, P66.
units.anchor: Providing students with reasoning for why AI will or will not be used

units.why: "Reinforcing expectations throughout the semester" asks for repeated communication beyond the syllabus, P66.
units.anchor: Reinforcing expectations throughout the semester to ensure students remain cognizant.
units.fit_note: Asks for repeated reminders rather than explanation of reasons.

units.why: "Modelling responsible AI use with students when use is appropriate" has instructors show responsible use, P112.
units.anchor: Modelling responsible AI use with students when use is appropriate for the course context.

units.why: "Overreliance on AI can: Weaken student skill development" gives the learning rationale for limits, P41.
units.anchor: Overreliance on AI can:
units.policy: Overreliance on AI can weaken student skill development, obscure authentic learning evidence and create academic integrity concerns.
units.fit_note: Also lists obscured learning evidence and integrity concerns.

units.why: "GenAI should support learning goals" ties AI use to learning goals, P83.
units.anchor: GenAI should support learning goals.

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to design assignments that emphasize process, reflection, iteration and critical engagement" recommends assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: design assignments that emphasize process, reflection, iteration and critical engagement

units.why: "When faculty use AI in teaching materials ... Be transparent where appropriate" asks faculty to disclose their own AI use, P47.
units.anchor: Be transparent where appropriate

units.why: "Follow disciplinary and publisher citation norms" for faculty AI use; P24 (cite AI use) applied to faculty, as P47 is disclosure to students.
units.anchor: Follow disciplinary and publisher citation norms
units.fit_note: Applies to faculty, not student submissions.

units.why: "Model ethical disclosure practices for students" frames faculty disclosure as modeling, P112.
units.anchor: Model ethical disclosure practices for students

units.why: "Faculty should not enter sensitive or restricted data into unapproved AI tools, including: student records or student work" restricts data entry, P50.
units.anchor: Faculty should not enter sensitive or restricted data into unapproved AI tools
units.policy: Faculty should not enter sensitive or restricted data into unapproved AI tools, including student records or student work, research data not approved for public sharing, and confidential, proprietary or protected information.

units.why: "USD’s preferred and approved platform for GenAI is Microsoft Copilot, while using a USD work or school account" prefers a vetted institutional tool, P92.
units.anchor: USD’s preferred and approved platform for GenAI is Microsoft Copilot

units.why: "Faculty should expect and plan for AI errors" asks faculty to expect wrong output, P31.
units.anchor: Faculty should expect and plan for AI errors.

units.why: "Review outputs for bias or omission" is a verification step, P31.
units.anchor: Review outputs for bias or omission

units.why: "Treat AI-generated content as suggestions, not authoritative answers" is a verification stance, P31.
units.anchor: Treat AI-generated content as suggestions, not authoritative answers

units.why: "This critical stance is essential for maintaining academic standards and modeling responsible use for students" ties verification to modeling, P112.
units.anchor: essential for maintaining academic standards and modeling responsible use for students

units.why: "GenAI can be useful in aiding course design activities" permits faculty AI use for course design, P59.
units.anchor: GenAI can be useful in aiding course design activities.

units.why: "Consider disclosing GenAI use to students to model transparency" recommends instructors disclose their AI use, P47.
units.anchor: Consider disclosing GenAI use to students to model transparency

units.why: "Review assessment instructions for clarity" is listed as a way faculty may use AI, P59.
units.anchor: Review assessment instructions for clarity.

units.why: "Generate sample prompts, discussion starters or practice questions" lists faculty AI uses for teaching materials, P59 (P48 would need disclosure/review language, which this lacks).
units.anchor: Generate sample prompts, discussion starters or practice questions.

units.why: "Create examples that students can critique or revise" is a faculty use of AI for teaching work, P59.
units.anchor: Create examples that students can critique or revise.

units.why: "Explore multiple explanations of complex concepts" is a faculty use of AI for teaching work, P59.
units.anchor: Explore multiple explanations of complex concepts.

units.why: "Support accessibility goals through generating alt text, creating alternative formats" names AI as an accessibility aid, P97.
units.anchor: Support accessibility goals through generating alt text, creating alternative formats

units.why: "GenAI should not replace faculty judgment, grading or evaluative decision-making" bars AI from grading, P46.
units.anchor: GenAI should not replace faculty judgment, grading or evaluative decision

units.why: "Student work and student data should not be entered into GenAI tools that are not approved for integrated use" restricts entering student work into unapproved tools, P50.
units.anchor: Student work and student data should not be entered into GenAI tools that are

units.why: "Reviewing faculty-drafted feedback language to help clarify action items" is a permitted, cautious use for feedback, P101 (conditions on AI-assisted feedback) since faculty draft first.
units.anchor: Reviewing faculty-drafted feedback language to help clarify action items for students
units.fit_note: Allowed use is to refine feedback the faculty member drafted.

units.why: "Identifying patterns in student responses so that more specific and substantive feedback can be provided" is a permitted feedback use, P59.
units.anchor: Identifying patterns in student responses so that more specific and substantive feedback

units.why: "Generating rubrics or criteria drafts" is a permitted faculty use, P59.
units.anchor: Generating rubrics or criteria drafts to help students better understand how work will be assessed.

units.why: "Support literature exploration or summary" lists AI for literature search in research, P104.
units.anchor: Support literature exploration or summary

units.why: "Assist with code, data cleaning or documentation" is a permitted research use; P89 is nearest for data cleaning.
units.anchor: Assist with code, data cleaning or documentation
units.fit_note: Also covers code and documentation help in research.

units.why: "Draft outlines or rephrase text for clarity" is a permitted writing-support use in research, P91.
units.anchor: Draft outlines or rephrase text for clarity

units.why: "Depending on disciplinary norms and publication expectations, AI may be used to enhance the research process" sets research AI rules by discipline and venue norms, P62.
units.anchor: Depending on disciplinary norms and publication expectations, AI may be used

units.why: "ensure all scholarly contributions remain grounded in their own expertise and analysis" keeps the researcher primary; P62 (research governance).
units.anchor: ensure all scholarly contributions remain grounded in their own expertise
units.fit_note: Also keeps the scholar the primary thinker (P32).

units.why: "adhere to ethical standards, disciplinary norms, intellectual property expectations and any sponsor, regulatory or data use requirements" defers to sponsor and regulatory rules, P62.
units.anchor: adhere to ethical standards, disciplinary norms, intellectual property expectations and any sponsor
units.fit_note: Also asks for rigorous validation of AI-generated content (P31).

units.why: "Protect sensitive, confidential or proprietary research data by using only approved tools and workflows" is a data rule for research, P50.
units.anchor: Protect sensitive, confidential or proprietary research data by using only approved tools and workflows.

units.why: "Document GenAI use to maintain transparency and integrity in the research record" asks faculty to document AI use in research; P24 applied to faculty.
units.anchor: Document GenAI use to maintain transparency and integrity in the research record.
units.fit_note: Applies to faculty research records, not student submissions.

units.why: "Misrepresenting GenAI-generated work as human-generated by students or faculty may raise academic misconduct under USD policy" classes misrepresentation as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Misrepresenting GenAI‑generated work as human‑generated by students or faculty may raise academic misconduct
units.fit_note: Misconduct is tied to misrepresenting AI work as human, not to AI use as such.

units.why: "rather than relying solely on detection tools, which are unreliable and raise privacy concerns" says detectors are unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: rather than relying solely on detection tools, which are unreliable and raise privacy concerns

units.why: Encouraging explicit academic-integrity conversations about GenAI is discussing the rules with students beyond the syllabus, P66.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to address GenAI explicitly as part of academic integrity conversations

units.why: "should be verified and human reviewed before decisions about academic misconduct are made" sets an evidence standard for tool scores, P69.
units.anchor: should be verified and human reviewed before decisions about academic misconduct are made

units.why: "No single indicator proves AI use" sets an evidence standard for AI-misuse findings, P69.
units.anchor: No single indicator proves AI use.

units.why: "multiple patterns together may warrant a conversation with the student" says to talk with the student first, P57.
units.anchor: multiple patterns together may warrant a conversation with the student

units.why: The lists of signs (polished but shallow, generic structure, missing or fabricated citations, confident inaccuracies) describe how to spot AI text by reading; P40 is the nearest type, though it covers software or logs.
units.anchor: Fluent writing with limited depth, original insight or disciplinary specificity.
units.policy: Signs that work may be AI-generated include fluent writing with limited depth, generic structure and language, missing, incorrect or fabricated citations, and confident inaccuracies.
units.fit_note: Describes reading-based indicators of AI text, not software, commit history or logs.

units.why: "the recommended next step is engagement and education, not accusation" prefers an educative response, P68.
units.anchor: the recommended next step is engagement and education, not accusation

units.why: "Asking students to explain or defend their work orally" checks understanding through explanation, P34.
units.anchor: Asking students to explain or defend their work orally.

units.why: "Requesting drafts, annotations, or reflections on decision-making" uses process evidence after suspicion; P40 rather than P26, which is students keeping logs in advance.
units.anchor: Requesting drafts, annotations, or reflections on decision-making.
units.fit_note: Asks students for drafts and reflections after suspicion (cf. P26).

units.why: "Having students identify challenges they faced and how they addressed them" is a reflection-based check of understanding, P34.
units.anchor: Having students identify challenges they faced and how they addressed them.
units.fit_note: Reflection on challenges rather than live questioning.

units.why: "These approaches support learning and academic integrity without relying on detection tools" says to avoid detector reliance, P39.
units.anchor: without relying on detection tools

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to frame concerns around learning outcomes, not tool use" ties integrity concerns to learning goals, P83.
units.anchor: frame concerns around learning outcomes, not tool use

units.why: "Can the student explain their reasoning and choices?" is a guiding question that checks student understanding, P30.
units.anchor: Can the student explain their reasoning and choices?
units.policy: Faculty should ask whether the student can explain their reasoning and choices.
units.fit_note: Framed as a question for faculty rather than a student duty.

units.why: "Assignments that emphasize process, iteration and reflection naturally reduce misuse" ties assignment design to preventing misuse, P35.
units.anchor: Assignments that emphasize process, iteration and reflection naturally reduce misuse

units.why: "Faculty should try to remain aware of these features and help students understand when AI is involved" covers AI embedded in common platforms, P07.
units.anchor: Faculty should try to remain aware of these features and help students understand
units.fit_note: Asks for awareness and explanation to students; it does not require disabling features.

units.why: "A tool may be using AI if it: Automatically rewrites, summarizes or expands content ..." defines how to recognize embedded AI, P61.
units.anchor: A tool may be using AI if it:
units.policy: A tool may be using AI if it automatically rewrites, summarizes or expands content, suggests sentences, explanations or solutions, generates content when clicking options like rewrite, improve or summarize, or produces polished responses without showing intermediate reasoning.

documents.unit: University of South Dakota (AI hub, Students)
documents.title: Generative AI Information: Students
documents.summary: Student guidance listing possible learning uses, core expectations (follow the instructor, do not substitute for learning, cite, protect data, verify) and how to recognize embedded AI.
documents.stance_why: The student page says "Follow Your Instructor’s Policies" and that "Some instructors allow AI freely; some allow it with limitations and others prohibit it", giving no stance of its own beyond core expectations.

units.why: Opening framing "Explore our guide to using new tools while keeping your work your own" signals encouragement with an ownership condition, P29 nearest.
units.anchor: keeping your work your own
units.fit_note: Frames the page as guidance for using new tools while keeping work one's own.

units.why: "When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to enhance learning" is a conditional permission that defers to context, so P04 is the structural type; specific uses are coded below.
units.anchor: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to enhance learning.
units.fit_note: Permission is conditional on context and discipline.

units.why: "Expand on ideas for projects or papers" is a listed learning use, brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: Expand on ideas

units.why: "Support finding or searching for resources, information, research etc. (research partner)" permits source finding, P104.
units.anchor: Support finding or searching

units.why: "Summarize complex readings or explain difficult concepts" permits explaining concepts (P12) and summarizing readings, which is the opposite of P105; the same page elsewhere says AI should not "replace reading course materials".
units.anchor: Summarize complex readings
units.fit_note: Also permits summarizing readings.

units.why: "Generate practice questions to study for exams" permits study aids, P14.
units.anchor: Generate practice questions

units.why: "Help organize notes to improve understanding of concepts" is a study aid use, P14.
units.anchor: Help organize notes

units.why: "Outline essays or presentations" is writing support, P91.
units.anchor: Outline essays or presentations

units.why: "Explore examples, such as sample code or problem-solving steps" permits looking at examples to learn, P12.
units.anchor: Explore examples,
units.policy: Students may use GenAI, when appropriate, to explore examples such as sample code or problem-solving steps.
units.fit_note: Sample code is named; submission of AI code is not addressed.

units.why: "Improve clarity in writing or refine drafts" permits editing support, P91.
units.anchor: Improve clarity

units.why: "it works best when you stay actively engaged, evaluate the output critically and make it your own" asks students to stay engaged and own the result, P32.
units.anchor: stay actively engaged, evaluate the output critically and make it your own

units.why: "While instructors may set more specific rules for their courses, here are core expectations" says university-wide expectations sit under instructor rules, P04.
units.anchor: While instructors may set more specific rules for their courses, here are core expectations

units.why: "Every class may have different rules" says each course sets its own rule, P11; the "models real-life use" clause adds a rationale.
units.anchor: Every class may have different rules; this is expected as it models real-life use
units.fit_note: Adds a rationale: varied rules model real-life use.

units.why: "Some instructors allow AI freely; some allow it with limitations and others prohibit it for certain assignments" describes the range of instructor choices, P04.
units.anchor: Some instructors allow AI freely; some allow it with limitations

units.why: "Always check the syllabus, assignment instructions or ask your instructor for AI guidelines" tells students to find and follow course rules, P78 (check syllabus first).
units.anchor: Always check the syllabus, assignment instructions or ask your instructor for AI guidelines.
units.fit_note: Also says to ask the instructor (P10).

units.why: "AI should not: Write your papers for you" bars having AI write submitted papers, P19.
units.anchor: Write your papers for you
units.policy: AI should not write your papers for you.

units.why: "Complete graded assignments that reflect your own understanding" bars AI from completing graded work, P19.
units.anchor: Complete graded assignments that reflect your own understanding
units.policy: AI should not complete graded assignments that reflect your own understanding.

units.why: "Replace reading course materials" bars using AI in place of reading; P105 is the nearest ban, but it says "replace", not a ban on all AI use with readings, and the page permits summarizing complex readings.
units.anchor: Replace reading course materials
units.policy: AI should not replace reading course materials.
units.fit_note: Bars replacing reading with AI; does not ban all AI use on readings, and the same page permits summarizing complex readings.

units.why: "Overreliance on AI can harm your learning and violate academic integrity policies" gives the learning rationale and links to integrity policy, P41.
units.anchor: Overreliance on AI can harm your learning and violate academic integrity policies.

units.why: "If you use AI to support your work, follow your course or program’s citation guidelines" requires citing per course rules, P24.
units.anchor: follow your course or program’s citation guidelines

units.why: "Common citation formats (APA, MLA, Chicago) now include ways to cite GenAI output" points to citation formats, P115.
units.anchor: Common citation formats (APA, MLA, Chicago) now include ways to cite GenAI output.

units.why: "when you use unprotected GenAI tools, the inputs or data you share might be used to train models" warns about data use by tools, P50.
units.anchor: the inputs or data you share might be used to train models

units.why: "Ensure you are using a protected platform when entering sensitive information" (own, others', instructor content, research data) is a privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: Ensure you are using a protected platform when entering sensitive information
units.policy: Ensure you are using a protected platform when entering sensitive information, such as your own private information, other students' information, instructor content or information, research data, and anything confidential or proprietary.

units.why: "USD's preferred and protected tool is Microsoft Copilot, though other tools are approved for limited use" prefers the vetted tool, P92.
units.anchor: USD's preferred and protected tool is Microsoft Copilot

units.why: "AI can sometimes: Create incorrect or misleading information; Fabricate citations; Present biased or incomplete answers" warns of errors, P31.
units.anchor: Create incorrect or misleading information
units.policy: AI can sometimes create incorrect or misleading information, fabricate citations and present biased or incomplete answers.

units.why: "Always check accuracy against trusted sources" tells students to verify output, P31.
units.anchor: Always check accuracy against trusted sources.

units.why: "Using GenAI in ways that misrepresent your own work may be considered academic misconduct under USD policy" classes misrepresentation as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Using GenAI in ways that misrepresent your own work may be considered academic misconduct
units.fit_note: Misconduct tied to misrepresenting own work.

units.why: "If you’re unsure whether something is acceptable, ask your instructor" is the ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: If you’re unsure whether something is acceptable, ask your instructor
units.fit_note: Also points to the Student Rights and Responsibilities site.

units.why: "Start with your own ideas before turning to AI" is a sequencing rule, P90.
units.anchor: Start with your own ideas

units.why: "Ask specific questions rather than vague ones" gives prompting advice, P93.
units.anchor: Ask specific questions

units.why: "Try multiple prompts to compare outputs" is prompting advice, P93.
units.anchor: Try multiple prompts to compare outputs.

units.why: "Verify sources and AI output" repeats the verification duty as a tip, P31.
units.anchor: Verify sources and AI output.

units.why: "Edit and personalize AI generated text" asks students to make AI text their own, P29.
units.anchor: Edit and personalize
units.policy: Students should edit and personalize AI-generated text.
units.fit_note: Frames ownership as editing AI text, which implies AI text may be used.

units.why: "Document what you used AI for (e.g., brainstorming, proofreading)" recommends documenting AI use, P24 as a tip rather than a requirement.
units.anchor: Document what you used AI for
units.fit_note: Presented as a tip, without saying where the documentation goes.

units.why: "Students should not assume that a tool does not use AI simply because it is familiar" covers AI built into everyday tools, P07.
units.anchor: should not assume that a tool does not use AI simply because it is familiar
units.fit_note: Asks for awareness; it does not require disabling features.

units.why: "If a tool is creating, rephrasing or predicting content for you, it is likely using AI" defines how to recognize AI features, P61.
units.anchor: If a tool is creating, rephrasing or predicting content for you

units.why: The list of signs ("Automatically rewrites, summarizes, paraphrases or expands text ... buttons such as suggest, improve, rewrite, solve, or summarize") defines what counts as AI-assisted features, P61.
units.anchor: Generates content when you click buttons such as
units.policy: A tool may be using AI if it automatically rewrites, summarizes, paraphrases or expands text, suggests sentences, answers or explanations rather than just formatting or checking spelling, generates content when you click buttons such as suggest, improve, rewrite, solve or summarize, produces polished responses without showing intermediate steps, or adapts responses based on your past behavior or inputs.

notes: Coder A. Course layer deferred; no school or computing-unit policy found. Hub, faculty and student pages overlap on some points; each coded on its own. The page statement that it is guidance and not official policy is UNCOVERED.
